newsitem.title: ITALY: Montedison, auditor ready to settle dispute.
newsitem.headline: Montedison, auditor ready to settle dispute.

text.p: Italian agro industrial group Montedison and auditors Price Waterhouse said they were ready to settle a dispute reaching back to 1993, with the auditors agreeing to pay out 51 billion lire.

In separate statements, Montedison and Price Waterhouse said the auditors would pay 31 billion lire to Montedison and 20 billion to its controlling company Compart, formerly known as Ferruzzi Finanziaria.
Price said the payments were not an acknowledgement of responsibility. The settlement must now be approved by shareholders of both Compart and Montedison.

Both Ferruzzi and Montedison went to the brink of collapse in 1993 following the discovery of huge debts. The companies are still controlled by a group of creditor banks which salvaged them at the time.
Price Waterhouse was the auditor in the years leading up to the collapse.

"We have dealt with a completely exceptional situation in which the issue of Ferruzzi, for which we recognise no responsibility, has been one of the most intricate of recent years," Sergio Duca, managing partner of Price Waterhouse Italia, said in the statement.
